title: Dynamic Arrays
concept: Arrays whose size is determined at runtime (based on user input)

steps.title: Include header files
steps.explanation:
We include `stdio.h` and `stdlib.h` for output and dynamic memory functions.

This lesson covers dynamic arrays whose size is determined at runtime.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created.

Unlike static arrays, dynamic arrays are allocated on the heap with a runtime-determined size.

steps.title: Declare size variable
steps.explanation:
We declare a `size` variable to hold the array length.

This value will be used later to calculate the malloc size.

steps.title: Print input prompt
steps.explanation: We print a prompt asking for the array length.

steps.title: Set size (simulated input)
steps.explanation:
In this example, we set the length with `size = 5`.

In practice, this is where user input would be received.

steps.title: Dynamic memory allocation (malloc)
steps.explanation:
`malloc(sizeof(int) * size)` creates a heap array that can store `size` integers.

The returned starting address is stored in pointer `arr` and used like an array.

steps.title: Initialize and print array with for loop
steps.explanation:
We fill in and print values using `arr[i]` syntax.

Dynamic arrays use the same index access method as static arrays.

steps.title: Free memory (free)
steps.explanation:
`free(arr)` returns the entire heap block at once.

After free, the heap memory is released but `arr` still holds the old address (dangling pointer). The dynamic array pattern is: allocate, use, then free at the end.

quiz.question: Which function is used to resize a dynamic array?
quiz.explanation: The `realloc(ptr, new_size)` function adjusts the memory size while preserving existing data (it even relocates if there is no room).

misconceptions.wrong: A dynamic array requires multiple calls to free
misconceptions.correct: You only need to free once.
misconceptions.why: Since you borrowed the entire block with a single `malloc` call, you return the entire block with a single `free` call.

keyTakeaway: When the size is unknown, use `malloc`. You can use array syntax ([]) on it just as conveniently.
